I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. That is the safest way for me to use the whole year, and it matches our local weather, irrigation habits, and what I can manage at my age without taking on too much risk. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable yield and better resistance, but I will keep the management simple and familiar. I will prepare the wheat field with rotary tillage, apply enough base fertilizer, irrigate a few key times, and control weeds and disease with a small number of pesticide sprays. After wheat harvest, I will quickly sow summer maize, use a bit more nitrogen for strong growth, irrigate when the weather is dry, and keep pesticide use limited unless pressure is obvious. I will not spread myself across too many crops, because I would rather manage two reliable grain crops well than chase a higher price with more labor and more uncertainty.
